name: Real-time graph databases for fraud rings
topic: Beava's current market position - competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against, evaluated against the use-case map in ../beava-use-cases/

competitive_landscape.incumbents: Two layers in the real-time-graph-for-fraud segment. (a) Standalone graph-DB vendors targeting fraud-ring detection as a flagship use case: Neo4j (>$200M ARR Nov 2024, ARR doubled over 3 years, 84% of Fortune 100, 58% of Fortune 500, dual-licensed GPL/AGPL+Commons-Clause community + commercial Enterprise + managed AuraDB and AuraDS, fraud-detection use case is one of the most-published verticals in their case-study library); TigerGraph ($174M total raised across 6 rounds, latest Series D-II from Cuadrilla Capital July 15 2025, hit by 30% layoffs (~90 staff) and four CEOs in four years, proprietary closed-source with a free Community Edition launched March 2025, 6+ hop traversals <100ms is the headline metric, JPMC/Mastercard/Microsoft/Unilever named customers, sub-second deep-link fraud-ring detection is the canonical positioning); Memgraph (BSL-1.1 source-available Community + proprietary MEL Enterprise starting $25K/yr/16GB, ~$11.4M total raised, In-Q-Tel + Heavybit investors, in-memory C++ Cypher-compatible engine, NASA + Cedars-Sinai + Capitec Bank named customers, claims 41x lower latency and 3-8x higher throughput vs Neo4j in their own Benchgraph, repositioning around GraphRAG/agentic-AI with Memgraph 3.0 in Feb 2025); ArangoDB (multi-model document+graph+key-value, $58.6M total raised, latest Corporate Minority from ORIX USA Aug 12 2025, Tazama-partnership fraud-detection benchmark Oct 2024, Apache-2.0 Community + commercial Enterprise); JanusGraph (fully Apache-2.0 Linux Foundation project, IBM/Google/Hortonworks-supported, distributed on Cassandra/HBase/Bigtable backends, G Data malware-graph and IBM-internal references, no commercial vendor behind it which both helps the OSS-posture conversation and limits the support-contract option). (b) Hyperscaler-bundled graph DBs that buyers can procure under an existing cloud relationship: Amazon Neptune + Neptune Analytics + the Oct 2025 GraphStorm GNN integration (real-time fraud-pattern detection bundled into AWS, train GNN models with GraphStorm and serve subgraph-neighborhood inference against Neptune Database); Azure Cosmos DB for Apache Gremlin; Google Cloud Spanner Graph + the Google Cloud Vertex AI + Neo4j AuraDS bundled partnership. The Redis-side graph option collapsed in Jan 2025 with RedisGraph reaching end-of-life and no plans for revival, removing what had been the obvious 'we already run Redis' on-ramp for fraud teams. The architectural pattern this segment has converged on for production CNP/APP fraud-ring detection - and the framing for beava - is a two-system stitched stack: a real-time feature/velocity layer (Redis+Lua, Aerospike, or in this market beava) plus a graph traversal layer (Neo4j / TigerGraph / Memgraph / Neptune) feeding the same downstream XGBoost/LightGBM/GNN scorer.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Domain-named graph-DB players actively pitching fraud-ring detection 2024-2026, with funding/scale evidence: Neo4j - >$200M ARR (Nov 2024 press release), management targeting ~$500M ARR within three years, the dominant graph-DB by mindshare and ecosystem (the public fraud-detection cookbook references span PaySim+GDS+Bloom and integrate with Snowflake Graph Analytics, AWS Neptune-style architectures, and Google Vertex AI); the Neo4j fraud-detection vertical is the most-cited case-study category on neo4j.com/use-cases/fraud-detection/, and a Fortune 500 financial-services case study running 2.2M txn/month is named publicly. TigerGraph - 600% ROI / $20.81M NPV Forrester TEI study, JPMC + Mastercard + Microsoft + Unilever named, 6+ hop fraud-ring traversals in milliseconds is the published headline, but the company is visibly weakened by 30% layoffs in 2024 + four CEO changes in four years + Glassdoor/Blind employee-stability concerns, and the July 2025 Cuadrilla Series D-II reads as bridge financing not growth capital; the free Community Edition launched March 2025 plus cloud-native pivot January 2025 are defensive moves against Neo4j+Memgraph+Neptune. Memgraph - $11.4M raised, the closest architectural shape to beava (in-memory, C++, single-process, push-on-event streaming via Pulsar/Kafka), explicit production fraud reference: Capitec Bank scoring 3.5M records/day through a GraphML fraud pipeline at 2.1% monthly average FPR with a Memgraph-backed knowledge graph linking transactions+customer profiles+device IDs+watchlists, end-to-end workflow ~2 hours; Memgraph 3.0 in Feb 2025 pivoted hard toward GraphRAG / agentic AI with vector search bundled in, which signals the fraud-vertical alone was not buying enough seats to sustain growth. Neo4j AuraDS - the managed-cloud Graph Data Science offering on Google Cloud and AWS, with Vertex AI bundling - is where Neo4j is pushing fraud-and-financial-services buyers who would otherwise self-host. ArangoDB - Tazama OSS-payments-fraud-platform benchmark October 2024 ('billions in digital transactions') is the public reference; multi-model story sells well into buyers that want to skip the (graph + document + KV) three-system stack. JanusGraph - no commercial vendor + free Apache-2.0 + distributed backends keeps it in the 'large-scale in-house build' segment (G Data malware-graph, IBM-internal) rather than the procurement-friendly enterprise tier. Amazon Neptune - hyperscaler-bundled, fraud-detection is one of three flagship use cases, GraphStorm GNN integration October 2025 closes a real gap (train + serve GNN models against the live OLTP graph). NebulaGraph and FalkorDB (Redis-Labs-spinout, fork of RedisGraph after EOL) and PuppyGraph are smaller players in the 2025-2026 landscape but don't yet have published fraud-vertical case studies at the scale of Neo4j/TigerGraph/Memgraph. CRITICAL framing: none of these are direct beava competitors - they perform graph traversal (multi-hop relationship discovery) which beava explicitly does NOT do; beava performs windowed aggregation per primary-key entity. The competition is in the architectural slot of 'how does the fraud team's stitched stack look', and the right pitch is 'beava + Memgraph (or TigerGraph or Neo4j) together replace Redis+Lua+Neo4j', not 'beava replaces Neo4j'.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Mixed and asymmetrically informative for beava. Neo4j: AGPLv3 + Commons Clause for Community Edition (the Commons Clause makes 'offer a product or service whose primary value is derived from Neo4j Community itself' a commercial-license trigger), proprietary commercial for Enterprise + AuraDB + AuraDS; effectively not-Apache-2.0 for downstream-product use. TigerGraph: fully proprietary closed-source with a free Community Edition (March 2025) - no OSS posture at all. Memgraph: BSL-1.1 (Business Source License 1.1) Community Edition with a four-year Change Date to Apache-2.0, proprietary MEL (Memgraph Enterprise License) for Enterprise - the BSL means the Community build is source-available but NOT Apache-2.0 for production-redistribution use; a vendor planning to sell a managed Memgraph-as-a-service runs into the BSL Additional Use Grant. ArangoDB: Apache-2.0 Community + commercial Enterprise (open-core, no rug-pull in 2024-2025 to date). JanusGraph: full Apache-2.0 Linux Foundation, no commercial entity (the cleanest OSS posture in the segment but also the smallest fraud-vertical footprint). Amazon Neptune: proprietary hyperscaler-managed, no OSS. With the Redis-Valkey split resolved in favor of Valkey for cloud-default Redis-API workloads, and with the BSL-relicensing pattern (Redis Stack 2024, Elastic 2018, MongoDB 2018, Materialize, Cockroach, HashiCorp) now a documented procurement risk pattern, beava's Apache-2.0 posture is a real differentiator for the graph-adjacent slot - against Memgraph (BSL-1.1 with future Apache-2.0 conversion), against Neo4j Community (AGPLv3+Commons-Clause), and against TigerGraph (proprietary). The narrow caveat: graph traversal itself is not on beava's roadmap, so the OSS-license wedge applies to the windowed-aggregation half of the stitched stack only.
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: Medium-to-High and rising. Amazon Neptune is now bundled into AWS spend with the October 2025 GraphStorm integration making 'train a GNN with GraphStorm + serve subgraph-neighborhood inference against Neptune Database' a few-clicks deployment; AWS Entity Resolution + Neptune Analytics is a published fraud-detection reference architecture. Google Cloud Vertex AI + Neo4j AuraDS is a co-marketed bundled offering (the Google Cloud blog references a productized integration). Azure Cosmos DB for Apache Gremlin is bundled into Azure subscriptions but lags on fraud-vertical marketing. The graph-DB hyperscaler-bundling threat is LESS severe than the feature-store / streaming-OLAP segments because graph databases are still seen as a specialist procurement (the buyer is the data-science / financial-crime-tech team, not the platform team) and the dedicated vendors (Neo4j, TigerGraph) have stronger ecosystem moats (Neo4j GDS algorithm library, Cypher standard, Bloom visualization) than the hyperscaler-managed equivalents. The 2025 RedisGraph EOL removed the 'we already pay Redis Enterprise, just use RedisGraph' bundled on-ramp, which paradoxically helps the standalone graph-DB vendors. For beava the relevance is indirect: the buyer who already lives in AWS is more likely to default to Neptune-on-AWS for the graph half of the stitched stack, which constrains beava's pitch to 'fit cleanly alongside Neptune as the feature substrate' rather than 'replace the whole stack with beava'.
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: Heterogeneous, dominated by Kafka and HTTP. Upstream into the graph DB: Kafka is universal at the production-fraud scale (Neo4j Streams / Neo4j Connector for Kafka is the canonical pattern; TigerGraph Kafka loader; Memgraph + Pulsar/Kafka streams; Neptune + Kinesis/MSK), with batch CSV/Parquet loaders for backfill. Some vendors expose Cypher / GSQL / Gremlin HTTP endpoints for direct event push, but the production reference architecture invariably has Kafka/Kinesis/Pulsar fronting the graph DB to absorb ingestion bursts and let the graph DB rebuild from the topic on cold start. Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 + framed-TCP :8081 push-on-event model is NOT a direct fit for the graph-DB ingestion path - the graph DB wants event-sourced topics, not direct entity pushes. The integration shape that works is: events land in Kafka, beava consumes Kafka for windowed-aggregation features, the graph DB consumes the same Kafka topic for relationship updates, both feed batch_get/Cypher-query reads into the scorer at decision time. This is the 'fan-out from Kafka to two specialized stores' pattern documented in Sardine's Fraud & Compliance Feature Store and Capitec Bank's GraphML fraud pipeline. Downstream consumers: the ML scorer (XGBoost / LightGBM dominant, GNN/GAT/StemGNN emerging per 2025 NVIDIA blog and arXiv 2411.05815 review) reads graph features (community ID, embeddings, node centrality, neighborhood aggregates) and beava features (per-entity velocities, n_unique, distance, distribution) in the same auth-time round-trip and combines them in the model. The rules engine (Drools / FEEL / vendor-specific DSL) likewise consumes both feature sets.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Both, with strong separation between the data path and the decisioning path. Graph DBs are typically used in two modes in production fraud rigs: (a) batch / micro-batch precomputation where Neo4j GDS or TigerGraph algorithms run community detection / PageRank / weakly-connected-components nightly or every-N-minutes and persist the resulting cluster/community labels as features the scorer reads at auth time; (b) point-traversal at decision time where the scorer issues a 'k-hop neighborhood around this card/account/device' query and feeds the result (n_unique counterparties at depth 2, max-clustering-coefficient, shortest-path-to-known-bad-entity) directly into the model. Beava sits below both, as the substrate for the windowed-aggregation feature set that the same scorer reads alongside the graph-derived features. The decisioning path is downstream of both - rules engine (hard caps, regulatory cut-offs) + ML scorer (XGBoost/LightGBM/GNN). The architectural invariant from beava's CLAUDE.md ('beava does NOT do graph traversal - it does windowed aggregations per entity') is exactly the boundary between the two systems.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: Beava's wedge in this segment is complementary, not competitive. The buyer in this slot is the fraud-engineering team that already has (or is procuring) a graph DB for ring/community/multi-hop detection and needs a windowed-aggregation feature substrate to live alongside it. Concrete reasons that buyer would pick beava over the Redis+Lua / Aerospike / Tecton patterns they would otherwise stitch to the graph DB: (1) Architectural shape match - beava is a single-binary in-memory push-on-event server, which is the closest architectural sibling to Memgraph in particular (both in-memory, both push-on-event, both with a Cypher-or-DSL declarative surface); the operator-mental-model cost of running beava + Memgraph is lower than beava + Neo4j or beava + TigerGraph. (2) ~60 first-class aggregation primitives natively cover counters, velocities, n_unique, distance, distribution - these are precisely the features that complement graph features (graph supplies 'shape of relationships', beava supplies 'rate of behavior'); the same scorer reads both. (3) Sub-millisecond TCP batch_get matches the ~100ms auth budget; Neo4j/TigerGraph/Memgraph Cypher queries at p99 are typically tens-of-ms for short traversals, leaving comfortable budget room. (4) Apache-2.0 with no Commons-Clause / BSL-1.1 / proprietary overhang is the only un-encumbered OSS posture in the feature-substrate slot adjacent to graph DBs (Memgraph is BSL-1.1, Redis Stack went BSL/RSAL in 2024 before the Valkey fork, RedisGraph EOL'd Jan 2025). (5) Push-on-event HTTP/JSON + framed-TCP avoids the Kafka requirement that Tecton / Feast / Hopsworks assume - a fraud team that already routes events into Kafka for the graph DB can dual-consume the same topic into beava; a fraud team that does NOT use Kafka (mid-market merchant, smaller PSP) can push directly into beava and dual-write the graph events into the graph DB via webhook-to-Kafka adapter or via the graph-DB HTTP ingest API. The framing for outbound pitches is explicit: 'beava + Memgraph (or TigerGraph or Neo4j) together replace the Redis+Lua+Neo4j stitched stack', not 'beava replaces a graph DB'.
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: The core disqualifier in this segment is structural, not solvable by feature work: beava does not and will not do graph traversal. The graph-traversal side of the stitched stack must be procured separately. Within the windowed-aggregation half that beava does claim, the gaps from V1/V2/V3 (CNP/APP/account-abuse) apply directly - (1) No TLS/auth on :8080/:8081/:8090 in v0 blocks any procurement-conscious bank/PSP/marketplace buyer the moment auditors look at the deployment. (2) No in-process sharding and ~684k EPS single-core / ~100-200 GB hot-state ceiling means beava is a per-region or per-tenant slice, not a global feature backend - acceptable for the design-partner sale, not for tier-1 global card networks. (3) No cross-region replication. (4) In-memory only with refuse-on-network-FS posture - WAL+snapshot recovery model; durable downstream sink for regulator-grade fraud-rate accounting is not in v0. (5) No triggers / no 'fire when counter crosses threshold' - particularly painful in the graph-adjacent slot because the production pattern is 'feature crosses threshold -> trigger k-hop graph query for ring detection -> feed cluster label back as a feature', and today beava cannot initiate that. (6) No multi-tenancy / namespace ACLs blocks the device-intel-vendor-hosted-tenant pattern (use case 20). (7) No secondary indexes / no scan API blocks the SOC-analyst hunter-query pattern that graph DB Bloom-style UIs serve natively. (8) No managed/hosted offering, no published integration runbook for beava + Neo4j or beava + Memgraph or beava + Neptune - which is the first piece of documentation a design-partner would ask for in this slot. (9) The graph-DB vendors all ship native fraud-detection demos / GraphSchool tutorials / Bloom visualizations / case-study libraries built up over 5-10 years; beava is two orders of magnitude behind on this developer/buyer-education surface.
beava_position_lens.time_to_credible_offering: 3-6mo for the design-partner shape (one buyer running beava + Memgraph or beava + Neo4j AuraDS as a stitched fraud stack with a published integration runbook). The graph-DB side is procured-not-built so the only beava-side engineering needed for the design partner is: TLS+auth (1-3mo, shared with V1/V2/V3), a published 'beava-features + Cypher-features -> XGBoost in 100ms' notebook against the canonical fraud event stream (~2-4 weeks if scoped tightly), and a kafka-consumer connector so beava can dual-consume the same topic the graph DB consumes (~4-8 weeks, not in v0). Triggers/action primitive (item 5 above) is a 1-3mo follow-on that strongly improves the graph-adjacent pitch. Cross-region replication and in-process sharding (6+ months) are NOT required for this segment - the graph-DB buyer is procurement-tolerant of regional/per-tenant deployments since they already run Neo4j Enterprise per-region clusters.

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: No beava-side proof points in the graph-adjacent slot, no published integration with Neo4j/Memgraph/TigerGraph/Neptune, no design partner that has paired beava with a graph DB for fraud-ring detection. Repo signals supporting the windowed-aggregation half are strong (python/beava/demos/fraud/ ships schema.json + events.jsonl, crates/beava-bench/configs/fraud-team.json is a tracked workload) but contain no graph-DB integration. Competitor-side evidence the architectural shape is real and growing: Capitec Bank + Memgraph (3.5M records/day, 2.1% monthly FPR, 9-account device-sharing rings discovered) is the closest public reference to the architectural shape beava would slot into; Sardine's Fraud & Compliance Feature Store (4,800 features, feature-store-feeds-rules-engine-plus-ML-engine pattern published explicitly) is the published reference for the 'feature substrate next to a graph store' shape; PayPal's billion-edges-per-day graph fraud writeups and the Neo4j fraud-detection cookbook are the published references for the graph-DB side. Funding/momentum signals on the graph-DB side: Neo4j >$200M ARR Nov 2024 with ARR-doubling-over-3-years; TigerGraph $174M raised total but weakened by 30% layoffs and CEO churn (the July 2025 Cuadrilla Series D-II reads more as bridge financing than growth capital); Memgraph repositioning hard around GraphRAG / agentic AI with Memgraph 3.0 in Feb 2025 (which is a Tell on the fraud-vertical-alone economics); ArangoDB Aug 2025 Corporate Minority from ORIX USA; the Oct 2025 Neptune+GraphStorm integration making hyperscaler-bundled GNN fraud detection meaningfully easier. Beava knows the buyer (fraud-engineering team at a merchant/marketplace/PSP/issuer/bank with an existing or planned graph-DB procurement) but has no published proof points and no integration runbook to that buyer yet.
